name: AR_DISTRIBUTION_SET_LINES_ALL
description: The AR_DISTRIBUTION_SET_LINES_ALL table stores specific information, such as GL account information, for individual distribution lines in a distribution set. Each row joins this accounting information with receipt distribution allocations. The total percent of all distribution set lines must equal 100% for each distribution set. Oracle Receivables creates one row for each receipt distribution percentage allocation. The AR_DISTRIBUTION_SETS_ALL table stores general information about your distribution set, such as the name, description, and status. Oracle Receivables uses distribution sets to speed data entry.  . The primary keys for this table are DISTRIBUTION_SET_ID and DIST_CODE_COMBINATION_ID.

columns.name: DISTRIBUTION_SET_ID
columns.description: Identifier of the individual distribution set line

columns.name: DIST_CODE_COMBINATION_ID
columns.description: Identifier of the accounting flexfield record associated with this distribution line

columns.name: SET_OF_BOOKS_ID
columns.description: General Ledger Set of Books used (only one currently supported)

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: PERCENT_DISTRIBUTION
columns.description: Percentage of payment to allocate to this distribution set account

columns.name: ORG_ID
columns.description: Indicates the identifier of the business unit associated to the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.
